description: Faction-specific narrative documents — orders, sermons, schedules, notices, directives — that reveal the daily texture of each faction's internal life. Covers underrepresented factions with no dedicated narrative files.

documents.transcript:
IRON GARRISON — PATROL ORDER 14
CLASSIFICATION: ROUTINE
DATE: Day 72, Year 3

PATROL: Alpha-3 (4 persons)
SECTOR: Southern perimeter, grid references 8-A through 12-D
DURATION: 36 hours
DEPARTURE: 05:00, Day 72
RETURN: 17:00, Day 73

OBJECTIVES:
1. Verify perimeter markers at posts 4, 7, and 11. Report any displacement.
2. Survey the southern road for caravan traffic. Log all parties observed — direction, size, cargo estimate.
3. Check the abandoned gas station at grid 10-C for new occupation signs.
4. Collect water samples from the creek crossing at grid 9-B. Submit to medical for rad count.

RULES OF ENGAGEMENT: Observe and report. No contact unless fired upon. No trade. No fraternization. Toll collection is authorized for parties exceeding two persons carrying visible cargo — refer to Tariff Schedule 6.

WEATHER: Ash storm forecast for Day 73 afternoon. Return before visibility drops below 50m.

— Sgt. Pell, Garrison Intake Officer
AUTHORIZED: Col. Voss (field stamp)

documents.title: Ash Militia — Council Agenda, Week 31
documents.material: Handwritten on recycled paper, pinned to a cork board
documents.physical_description: Paper is the back of a pre-war flyer. Written in pencil, large letters for readability. Pin holes in all four corners. A child has drawn a small sun in the margin.
documents.transcript:
ASH MILITIA — COUNCIL AGENDA
Week 31, Day 89
ALL MEMBERS WELCOME. VOTING OPEN TO REGISTERED HEADS OF HOUSEHOLD.

1. Ration allocation review — current shortfall is 8%. Proposal: reduce evening meal by one ladle across all households until the greenhouse harvest comes in. Discussion.

2. Defence rotation — two sentries dropped out last week (illness, not refusal). Need volunteers for the north watch, 22:00-04:00, three nights per week. Suki has offered the greenhouse shift as a swap.

3. Trade proposal from the Railway Guild — they want water access in exchange for vacuum tubes and copper wiring. Do we have water to trade? Discussion with the Hydro Barons' current delivery schedule.

4. New arrivals — two persons requesting registration. Screening complete (medical clear, no weapons beyond one knife each). Vote on admission.

5. Any other business.

— Posted by the Militia Council Secretary

documents.title: Sermon Fragment — 'The Weight of Ash'
documents.material: Written on the back of a pre-war poster, charcoal on plasterboard
documents.physical_description: Board is 60cm by 40cm, broken along one edge. Text is written in charcoal, large block letters. Several passages are underlined with a red crayon. The board was likely mounted on a wall or carried as a sign.
documents.transcript:
THE WEIGHT OF ASH

You think the ash is punishment. You are wrong.
The ash is a question.

What did you build that the fire could not burn?
What did you hoard that the wind could not scatter?
What did you love that the silence could not answer?

The ash falls on the just and the unjust.
The ash does not distinguish.
This is not cruelty. This is honesty.

We who carry the Ash Sign do not worship destruction.
We witness what destruction revealed.

Before the fire, we built towers and called them progress.
We filled warehouses and called them security.
We drew borders and called them peace.

The ash showed us the truth:
Nothing we built was strong enough.
Nothing we hoarded was real enough.
Nothing we drew was deep enough.

The ash is the question.
Your answer is how you live beneath it.

— Spoken at the gathering, Day 44. Recorded by a listener.

documents.title: Dead Hand Communication Protocol — Extract
documents.origin: Laminated card from the sub-basement cache
documents.physical_description: Card is 8cm by 12cm, sealed in heat-pressed plastic. Text is printed in monospaced type, very small. A punch hole in one corner suggests it was carried on a ring with other protocol cards.
documents.transcript:
DEAD HAND COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL — EXTRACT
AUTHORITY LEVEL: 3 (FIELD OPERATIVES)

FREQUENCY SCHEDULE:
- Primary: 142.5 MHz, broadcast at 03:00 and 15:00 local
- Secondary: 88.4 MHz, broadcast at 06:00 and 18:00 local
- Emergency: 156.8 MHz, continuous listen only

BROADCAST FORMAT:
- Five-digit group repeated three times
- Followed by two-letter designator
- Followed by single digit (1-5) for priority level
- No voice. No Morse. Numbers only.

RESPONSE PROTOCOL:
- If you hear your cell's designator: acknowledge with three short bursts on secondary frequency within 1 hour
- If you hear priority 5: initiate denial procedures immediately
- If you hear nothing for 72 consecutive hours: assume compromise. Scatter. Go dark. Do not attempt contact.

NOTE: This card is self-authenticating. No additional credentials required. Destroy if captured.

documents.title: Quiet House — Guest Rules
documents.origin: Posted at the entrance door, the_approach
documents.material: Handwritten on cotton paper, framed behind glass
documents.physical_description: Paper is the same handmade stock as the registry pages. Ink is iron gall. The glass frame is salvaged — one corner cracked and taped. The text is centered, with generous margins.
documents.transcript:
THE QUIET HOUSE — RULES FOR GUESTS

1. You are welcome here. You do not need to explain why you came.
2. You may stay one night. Two if you are injured or the weather is dangerous. Three only by agreement.
3. We will give you water. We will give you food if we have it. We will give you a dry place to sleep.
4. We will not ask your name. You may tell us if you wish.
5. We will not ask where you are going. You may tell us if you wish.
6. We will not ask where you have been. You may tell us if you wish.
7. Do not steal. Do not fight. Do not bring your wars through our door.
8. If you are sick, tell us. We have a medic. She is good.
9. If you die here, we will bury you with care. Your belongings will be kept for one year. If no one claims them, they go to the next person who needs them.
10. The door is unlocked during daylight. It is locked at night. If you arrive after dark, knock three times. We will hear you.

— The Quiet House

documents.transcript:
OVERLAY ROUTE ASSESSMENT — CORRIDOR 7
Surveyor: Maren Holt
Date: Day 78, Year 3

ROUTE: Toll Gate junction → Ridgecrest → Saltworks Siding
DISTANCE: 14.2 km (measured by wheel)
ELEVATION CHANGE: +180m net ascent, +40m descent at midpoint
SURFACE: Broken asphalt (40%), packed dirt (35%), scree (25%)
WATER: One seasonal creek crossing at km 6.8. Unreliable after Day 60.
RADIATION: Baseline 8-14 uSv/h along entire corridor. One hotspot at km 9.2 (22 uSv/h, 50m radius — mark and avoid).
SHELTER: None along route. Emergency shelter possible at km 4.5 (collapsed building, partial roof).
THREATS: Warlord patrol activity reported between km 10-12. Scavenger parties observed at km 2-3 (non-hostile).

RECOMMENDATION: Corridor 7 is viable for foot travel with light loads during daylight hours. Not recommended for night travel or solo parties. Mark as SECONDARY on the master overlay.

— Maren Holt, Overlay Surveyor

WATER COURT OF THE SALT FREEHOLDERS

SUMMONS: Any party extracting water from the southern drainage basin is summoned to appear before the Water Court on Day 92, at the Saltworks Siding marker.

CHARGE: Unauthorized extraction from a claimed water source (Brine Accord, Year 2, Section 4).

EVIDENCE: Footprints and digging marks observed at the creek crossing (grid 9-B) on Day 79. Volume extracted estimated at 20+ litres.

PENALTY UPON FINDING: Forfeiture of water rights for one season. Alternative: payment of 10 litres clean water to the Freeholders' common store.

FAILURE TO APPEAR: Water rights revoked permanently. Trespass designation applied to the party's home settlement.

— Leva Quist, Shift Lead, on behalf of the Freeholders' Council

documents.material: Typed on pre-war military form, stamped
documents.physical_description: Form is standard 15cm by 20cm. Typed in black with red ink classification stamp. Folded into thirds. A handwritten annotation in pencil at the bottom reads: 'Effective Day 70 — supersedes Schedule 5.'
documents.transcript:
IRON GARRISON — TARIFF SCHEDULE 6
TRANSIT TOLLS — SOUTHERN PERIMETER
Effective: Day 70, Year 3

PARTIES OF 1-2 PERSONS (NO CARGO):
- Transit pass: 1 x iodine pill OR 1 x battery OR equivalent value
- Valid for 24 hours, single direction

PARTIES OF 3-5 PERSONS (WITH CARGO):
- Transit pass: 10% of cargo by weight
- Minimum: 5 litres clean water OR 20 rounds ammunition (any calibre)
- Valid for 48 hours, single direction

PARTIES OF 6+ PERSONS:
- Contact Garrison Command directly. Group rates negotiable.
- Escort available at additional cost (1 person per 4 travellers)

EXEMPTIONS:
- Garrison personnel on duty (carry valid ID)
- Medical emergencies (carry proof — medic's note or visible injury)
- Railway Guild scheduled transports (carry Guild transit pass)

ENFORCEMENT: Toll evasion is classified as theft of Garrison resources. Penalty: confiscation of cargo. Repeat offence: 72-hour detention.

— Sgt. Pell, Garrison Intake Officer
AUTHORIZED: Col. Voss (field stamp)

documents.title: Cult of the Ash Sign — Burial Rite for the Irradiated
documents.origin: Recited at the gathering, transcribed by a listener
documents.material: Written on the back of a pre-war map, charcoal on paper
documents.physical_description: Map is a road atlas page — the reverse side is covered in charcoal writing. The text is arranged in stanzas with line breaks, suggesting it is meant to be spoken aloud. A thumbprint of red ochre marks the top left corner.
documents.transcript:
BURIAL RITE FOR THOSE WHO GLOW

(To be spoken at the graveside when the deceased carried more than 50 mSv lifetime dose)

We return you to the ash.
You carried the light inside you.
It was not yours. It was never yours.
The ash gave it. The ash takes it back.

We do not fear the light.
We do not curse the light.
The light is the ash's memory of what you were.

Your skin held the sun.
Your bones held the earth.
Your breath held the wind.
Now all three return to where they began.

We mark this place.
We do not seal it.
The ash must be free to fall here.
The wind must be free to carry what remains.

Go gently.
The ash remembers you.
The ash will always remember.

(Spoken by the Reader. The congregation responds in silence. A dosimeter is placed on the grave and left to count down.)

REBUILDERS — LABOUR CALL
Week 32, Day 91

ALL ABLE-BODIED RESIDENTS: The following work details are posted for the coming week. Sign up with Mattis Cray at the Council Hall by 18:00 tonight.

ROAD CREW (4 persons): Eastern approach repair. Gravel hauling, surface levelling. Heavy work. 3 days minimum. Boots required.

WATER CREW (2 persons): Trench extension, southern cluster. Clay pipe laying, joint sealing. Moderate work. 2 days.

SORTING CREW (3 persons): Salvage pile sorting and allocation. Light work. Suitable for all ages 14+. 1 day.

GUARD CREW (2 persons): Perimeter watch rotation. Night shift, 22:00-06:00. Armed. Must be 16+ and pass the vision check.

NOTE: Labour call is mandatory for all registered residents who have not contributed labour in the past 14 days. Exemptions: medical (bring note from the medic), childcare (children under 6), or assigned to another detail.

FOOD PROVIDED: Midday meal for all work crews. Extra half-ration for heavy labour details.

— Cael Ormund, Registrar-General

documents.title: Hydro Barons — Aquifer Level Report, Month 7
documents.material: Typed on recycled paper, with hand-drawn cross-section diagram
documents.physical_description: Two sheets of paper, stapled. First sheet is the report text. Second sheet is a hand-drawn cross-section of the aquifer with water level markings in blue pencil. The diagram is surprisingly precise — someone with engineering training drew it.
documents.transcript:
HYDRO BARONS — AQUIFER LEVEL REPORT
Month 7, Year 3
Prepared by: Leva Quist, Shift Lead

STATION 4 ARTESIAN WELL:
- Current water table: 12.4m below surface (down from 11.8m last month)
- Drawdown rate: 0.6m per month (stable — within seasonal expectation)
- Yield: 80 litres per day (sustainable at current extraction rate)
- Quality: Clear. No sediment. Rad count 0.3 uSv/L (within safe range).

STATION 7 SHALLOW WELL:
- Current water table: 4.1m below surface (down from 3.6m last month)
- Drawdown rate: 0.5m per month (slightly elevated — monitor)
- Yield: 40 litres per day (reduced from 50 due to sediment increase)
- Quality: Slight turbidity. Requires settling before delivery. Rad count 0.8 uSv/L.

RECOMMENDATION: Station 7 yield reduction is temporary — sediment flush expected within 2 weeks. If drawdown exceeds 0.7m/month for two consecutive months, reduce delivery schedule by 20%.

CUSTOMER NOTICE: Delivery prices remain unchanged for Month 8. Early payment discount still available.

— Leva Quist, Hydro Barons

documents.transcript:
ASH MILITIA — DEFENCE ALERT
CONDITION: YELLOW

EFFECTIVE: Day 86, 14:00

REASON: Warlord patrol observed within 2km of the southern perimeter. Three persons, armed, moving east along the ridge. No contact made. No shots fired.

ACTION REQUIRED:
- All sentry posts doubled until further notice
- All residents within 500m of the southern perimeter prepare to relocate to the community hall if ordered
- Weapons locker opened — one rifle per assigned defender, ammunition distributed
- Children moved to the interior schoolroom. School suspended until Condition Green.
- Greenhouse shift continues — Suki's team is exempt from relocation

COMMUNICATION: Check the notice board every 2 hours. Do not spread rumours. Report sightings to the duty officer — do not investigate alone.

CONDITION GREEN WILL BE POSTED WHEN THE PATROL IS CONFIRMED CLEAR OF THE AREA.

— The Militia Council
